issuer: the General Directorate of Traffic, Ministry of Interior
note: Read 2026-10-30: 'Road safety in Qatar: provisions and penalties' by David Salt and Emma Higham (a Doha law firm's column, Gulf Times, 26 February 2013), summarising the Traffic Law (Law No. 19 of 2007) in their own translation: a driver's licence applicant must be over 18 and pass the examination; Qataris' licences were then issued for 10 years, non-Qataris' for five. Marked secondary, quoting the law on Al Meezan (almeezan.qa, the Ministry of Justice's legal portal, now a script-rendered site whose law pages weren't reached). The age is held (the law's own requirement, as the column states it). The term is not: the column is from 2013 and no current source was read to confirm 10 years still holds, so validYears is null (the 10 and 5 years are the 2013 reading). Fee: none found (Hukoomi, the government portal, answered a maintenance page; the Ministry of Interior's portal renders its services by script and gave none): null. The issuer is the Ministry of Interior's General Directorate of Traffic, by its own portal's list of directorates (its Licensing Affairs Department). No identity card is issued by the directorate; the column's exemptions for GCC licences are a right to drive, not an exchange list, and aren't held.

sources.title: Gulf Times, Road safety in Qatar: provisions and penalties (David Salt and Emma Higham, 26 February 2013)
sources.said: Applicants must be Qatari, over 18 years of age, in good health, not convicted of a crime and must have passed the current examination requirements. ... Licences for Qataris are issued for 10 years, for non-Qataris five years (renewable)
